To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IRAC colours of submm/mm galaxy counterparts are distinct from the general galaxy population.

the use of a non-parametric characteristic density distribution of Spitzer IRAC colour–colours allows us to rank potential counterparts to submm/mm sources, and that this technique can be used for all observations with a positional uncertainty of 10 arcsec or less, and for all radio-quiet observations.

(1) IRAC colours are a useful discriminator between likely counterparts and general IRAC galaxy populations, (2) a non-parametric colour–colour characteristic distribution is the most effective method for using this information, (3) the reliability of this method can be improved with positional uncertainty information and (4) this technique is an effective tool for identifying counterparts to SMGs and other submm/mm galaxies.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the IRAC colour–IRAC colour distribution of SMG counterparts is distinct from the general IRAC population, and that this information, when combined with a positional likelihood ratio, allows us to identify robust and tentative SMG counterparts with a reliability of >90 per cent for observations with moderate beam sizes.
a simple non-parametric IR colour–colour density distribution is an excellent discriminator between SMG counterparts and the general galaxy population.
